original_question: Determine whether the cubic Diophantine equation 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 has an integer solution.
target_in_paper: Section 7, equation (39), read together with Problem 6 in Section 6: decide whether 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 has an integer solution; the paper identifies it as the shortest cubic equation with open Problem 6. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))
correct_elements: Your draft already uses the exact equation from the paper and asks the correct kind of question—mere existence of an integer solution, not finiteness, infinitude, parametrization, or positivity. This is precisely Problem 6 specialized to equation (39). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))
missing_details: Make the quantifiers explicit: ask whether there exist integers x, y, z ∈ ℤ satisfying the equation, rather than leaving the domain implicit in the phrase 'integer solution.' ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))

State that no extra restrictions are imposed: the paper does not require x, y, z to be positive, nonzero, primitive, or distinct. It is an unrestricted integer-solvability question under Problem 6. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))

If you want full paper-faithful context, note that this is equation (39) in Section 7 and is singled out there as the shortest cubic equation for which Problem 6 is open; its length is l = 9 + log_2 21 ≈ 13.4. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))
refined_question: Decide whether there exist integers x, y, z ∈ ℤ such that 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. Section 6 defines Problem 6 as determining whether a Diophantine equation has an integer solution, and Section 7 then identifies 7x^3 + 2y^3 = 3z^2 + 1 as equation (39), the shortest cubic equation in the paper for which Problem 6 is open. So the faithful refinement is simply to make the quantifiers over ℤ explicit and avoid adding any stronger requirement such as finding all solutions or proving infinitude. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.08518))
